discoveries.headline: A Kohlmann family owned the village inn at Kleindehsa near Löbau from 1787 to 1959, beside the hamlet of Kötzschau. No link to this family is proven yet.
The firm Weickert & Eifler had the wartime company number 0/0156/5156, stamped on its 1943 invoice. What it supplied is not yet known.
discoveries.source: Weickert & Eifler invoice, 9 April 1943, and a collectors' register of Reichs-Betriebs-Nummern
discoveries.imageAlt: The stamped company number on the Weickert and Eifler invoice of 9 April 1943.

discoveries.headline: The family chart names Alwin Eifler's brothers Max and Alfred and his sister Martha.
Ernst Eifler, a farmer at Sohland, was probably the father of Alwin, Max, Alfred and Martha Eifler. A birth entry would prove it.
discoveries.source: Marriage register, Standesamt Dresden V, 1926 Nr. 352, and the 2007 family chart
discoveries.imageAlt: Alwin Eifler and Gertrud Becker's 1926 marriage entry, Dresden V Nr. 352.

discoveries.headline: The family chart names Richard Becker's sister Marie, married name perhaps Wettlitz, at Rothermundtstraße 5 in Dresden.
Richard Becker had a second sister. Her name is not on the page of the family chart the family holds.
Christa Eifler's husband, married at Bautzen in 1952, was Herbert Kohlmann, called Herbert Coleman in English. The name Alvin belonged to Christa's father, Alwin Eifler.
discoveries.changeNote: The site had given Christa's husband the first name Alvin.
discoveries.source: Family correction, 26 November 2026, given by the family

discoveries.headline: The family named another grandchild of Herbert and Christa Kohlmann, a son of one of their two sons. He is on the tree.
discoveries.source: Family testimony, 27 November 2026, given by the family

discoveries.headline: A 1969 note on Alwin Eifler's marriage entry shows that his death on 18 December 1968 was registered at Zittau, which is why Bautzen has no record of it.

source.text: Marriage register Dresden V, 1926 Nr. 352, margin note (Ancestry)

discoveries.imageAlt: The 1969 margin note on Alwin and Gertrud Eifler's 1926 marriage entry, recording his death at Zittau.

discoveries.headline: Another researcher's tree names more Kohlmanns of Kleindehsa: Maria Alwine (1868 to 1900) and her parents Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann and Christiane Kriegel. Her father may be the innkeeper Ernst Kohlmann. No link to this family is proven.
A second researcher's tree has Johanne Sophie Helene Kohlmann of Kleindehsa, who married at Cunnewalde and named her son, born in 1857, Karl Friedrich Ernst. No link to this family is proven.

discoveries.imageAlt: Alwin Eifler and Gertrud Becker's 1926 marriage entry, Dresden V Nr. 352.
discoveries.headline: The original entry for Alwin Eifler and Gertrud Becker's wedding in Dresden on 2 October 1926: he was a manufacturer of Wendischer Graben 3, Bautzen, born at Sohland an der Spree; she was 21, of Rothermundtstraße 5.

source.text: Marriage register Dresden V, 1926 Nr. 352 (Stadtarchiv Dresden, via Ancestry)

discoveries.imageAlt: Gertrud Elise Becker's 1905 birth entry, Dresden I Nr. 165.
discoveries.headline: Gertrud Becker's birth entry: born at home, Ziegelstraße 2 in Dresden, on 22 January 1905; her father, the merchant Richard Hermann Becker, reported it five days later and signed it.

source.text: Birth register Dresden I, 1905 Nr. 165 (Stadtarchiv Dresden, via Ancestry)

discoveries.imageAlt: Richard Becker's entry in the 1903 Dresden address book.
discoveries.headline: Richard Becker ran his own grocery and drugstore on the ground floor of Ziegelstraße 2 in Dresden by 1903, the house where his daughter Gertrud was born two years later.

source.text: Adreßbuch für Dresden und seine Vororte 1903 and 1905 (SLUB Dresden)

discoveries.headline: The Sohland church book names Alwin Eifler's parents: Ernst Gustav Eifler, a baker, and Johanna Christiane née Kahden. His sister Martha was born in the same house in 1890 and died in 1932.

source.text: Kirchgemeinde Sohland/Spree, church books 1890 Nr. 18 and 1892 Nr. 154 (extract sent to the family, 27 November 2026)

discoveries.imageAlt: The commercial register notice of December 1922 for Weickert & Eifler.
discoveries.headline: Weickert & Eifler was founded as a partnership on 11 October 1922 by the master saddler Bruno Weickert and the merchant Alwin Eifler, at An den Fleischbänken 7 in Bautzen.

discoveries.imageAlt: The commercial register notice of January 1923.
discoveries.headline: Only three months later, in January 1923, Bruno Weickert left the firm, and Alwin Eifler carried on alone under the old name.

discoveries.imageAlt: Newspaper report listing Weickert und Eifler's steel-wire mattresses at the Industriehof exhibition.
discoveries.headline: In June 1922 Weickert & Eifler's steel-wire mattresses were on show at the opening of the Industriehof Gnaschwitz, a munitions works being turned over to peacetime trades.
In the hyperinflation autumn of 1923 the firm advertised in a Munich export weekly: "Export to all countries! Agents abroad wanted."

source.text: "Ost und Süd", 8 September to 15 December 1923 (Deutsches Zeitungsportal)

discoveries.imageAlt: News item on the master saddlers' examination of April 1920.
discoveries.headline: Bruno Weickert passed his master saddler's examination on 21 April 1920, back from the war like all five candidates.

discoveries.imageAlt: Baptism entry for Ernestine Marianne Kohlmann, December 1914.
discoveries.headline: Alwin Kohlmann, then a journeyman butcher in Bautzen, had a daughter on 19 November 1914, baptised Ernestine Marianne.

source.text: Bautzener Nachrichten, 28 November and 30 December 1914 (SLUB Dresden)

discoveries.imageAlt: Casualty list line for Hermann Kohlmann of Kleindehsa.
discoveries.headline: Hermann Kohlmann of Kleindehsa, born 1897, was reported missing with Infantry Regiment 107 and later found to be a prisoner of war.

discoveries.imageAlt: Dresdner Journal item of 1856 about J. T. Kohlmann.
discoveries.headline: In 1856 Johann Traugott Kohlmann was both butcher and innkeeper at Kleindehsa, and thieves kept stealing the hides drying in his slaughterhouse loft.

discoveries.imageAlt: Newspaper line naming the Kretscham owner Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann.
discoveries.headline: Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann owned the Kleindehsa Kretscham in 1874, so he was very probably the innkeeper Ernst of the village chronicle.

source.text: Bautzener Nachrichten, 5 December 1874 and 14 March 1885 (SLUB Dresden)

discoveries.imageAlt: Court notice of the 1889 sale of the Kretscham.
discoveries.headline: In April 1889 the court auctioned the Kretscham, almost 8 hectares with the inn, from the estate of Christiane Elisabeth Kohlmann née Kriegel.

discoveries.imageAlt: Local news item of April 1913 about Reinhold Kohlmann's son.
discoveries.headline: Reinhold Kohlmann of Kleindehsa was a master butcher and cattle dealer; in 1913 his eldest son, 19, fractured his skull when his cart overturned on a steep hill.

discoveries.imageAlt: List of new master butchers, November 1925.
discoveries.headline: A younger Reinhold Kohlmann of Kleindehsa, probably the son, passed the master butcher's examination in 1925.

discoveries.imageAlt: Court report of 1931 naming the Gasthaus von Kohlmann.
discoveries.headline: In the 1920s and 1930s the inn was known as Kohlmanns Gasthof; a court report of 1931 names it as the place where a political training course ate supper.

The oldest Kohlmann papers found so far: two court files in the Saxon State Archives, a Christian Kohlmann of Kötzschau in 1807 and Gottfried Kohlmann of Kleindehsa in 1824, both quarrelling over village duties.

source.text: Sächsisches Staatsarchiv, 50151 Gutsherrschaft Kleindehsa Nr. 11 and 50009 Oberamtsregierung Nr. 2887

discoveries.imageAlt: Casualty list line for Ernst Jurack of Briesing.
discoveries.headline: Two Jurack men from Briesing, Marie Ida's home village, appear in the First World War casualty lists: Ernst, killed in 1915, and Gustav, a prisoner who came home. A family link is not proven.

source.text: Verlustliste Sachsen Nr. 200, 1915, and later lists (des.genealogy.net)

discoveries.imageAlt: Casualty list line for Sergeant Max Woltmann of Mittweida.
discoveries.headline: A Sergeant Max Woltmann of Mittweida, near Döbeln, was wounded in 1914. He may be the Döbeln tax official, but that is not proven.
